rationale: Review started 2026-11-10T06:54:52Z and ended 2026-11-10T07:05:36Z (UTC). I re-hashed the held texts jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_9674.txt and EO_9744.txt (both equal their recorded text_sha256, and every source fingerprint matches) and confirmed that the ORIGINAL, ACT and ACTOR_TEXT spans equal their recorded text. I read EO 9674 (11 FR 333, signed January 4, 1946, Liquidation of War Agencies) in full and confirmed its identity against the OFR catalog record: paragraphs 1-4 create a Director of Liquidation and a Liquidation Advisory Committee in the Office for Emergency Management, set the Director's duties (a)-(f), add a proviso that other agencies keep their own liquidation functions, and give the Director staffing power, with no own-terms end. EO 9744 (11 FR 7255, signed June 27, 1946) provides that the office of the Director of Liquidation and the Liquidation Advisory Committee, 'established by Executive Order No. 9674 of January 4, 1946, together with the functions of the Director and the Committee, are hereby terminated' and that 'This order shall become effective on June 30, 1946'; it names this order and reaches every operative command in it, because paragraph 3 only preserves other agencies' functions and the records-disposition direction is EO 9744's own command. A cruden number search of held order texts found EO 9674 cited only by EO 9744 (FR and APP copies), so I found no earlier revocation, supersession or parent end and no revival; the U.S. Code and eCFR machine searches had 0 hits and the history has no flags to resolve. The recommended status NO, ended effective June 30, 1946, is supported by held sources through 2026-10-14.
